newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ex-Frankfurt rates, demand up to Asia, N.America.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Frankfurt rates, demand up to Asia, N.America.

text.p: Air cargo market rates in Germany have picked up in reaction to an autumn upturn in demand and a Lufthansa rates increase, a Reuters' market survey showed.
Prices to Asia where demand for Korea, Japan and south-east Asia is rising strongly, have risen by more than 10 percent on some routes.

Some North American destinations are also slightly more expensive with the end of cheap, ad-hoc rates offered to fill cargo capacity generated by additional summer holiday passenger traffic, research revealed.
New Lufthansa prices taking effect on October 1 included increases of just under 10 percent to Bangkok, Singapore and Hong Kong, and weight-related rises of five percent to Brazil and Canada.

Several leading non-European airlines operating out of Germany, including Singapore Airlines, Cathay Pacific and Varig, have followed with increases of between five and ten percent on selected routes.
But some European rivals such as Air France and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines are continuing to compete in Germany on price, sources said.

Lufthansa Cargo Germany director Joachim Steinbach said: "We are optimistic we can push through the rates increase. We have set a signal and we are very confident that the last three months of the year will be good.
"All the forwarders expect a good autumn and I think we can look forward to a stable autumn which we need after the poor start to the year," he added.
Steinbach said: "We can only call upon Air France and KLM not to sell through (lower) prices."
Florian Pfaff, Lufthansa Cargo sales and marketing manager Germany, added: "We are not very happy that Air France and KLM will not increase rates and that is hurting."
Rates up to south-east Asia have risen across the board and are holding firm to Japan, Korea and China, research showed.
Capacity to south-east Asia will rise substantially this autumn when Singapore Airlines and Lufthansa virtually double their capacity from Frankfurt to Singapore to 400 tonnes weekly.
The two airlines will start two additional Boeing 747-200F services via Sharjah from October 31.
Thai Airways cargo sales manager Germany, Guillermo Valencia, welcomed higher market rates to Bangkok as these now approached the unchanged, higher Thai Airways levels.
"Clients must accept these higher rates because everyone has increased prices," he said.
Valencia added: "We have very positive expectations for the autumn. It is not a boom but we see the normal growth from October to Christmas."
The airline's new, weekly B747-200 freighter, replacing one of the two all-cargo flights of partner Lufthansa, was currently departing Frankfurt virtually full, he pointed out.
The Germany sales manager of an Asian carrier said: "We have increased rates but it is too early to say if it can be carried through in the market."
He added: "September was an average month. We expect and hope it will increase a little now but we do not expect boom growth."
Rates to Japan and Korea have firmed slightly in September and early October on the strength of rising volumes although competition remains strong, market sources said.
Meinolf Weiden, Nippon Cargo Airlines sales manager, said: "Our flights are full. We have a 100 percent load factor to Japan and have reached our revenue, tonnage and yield budgets."
NCA decided not to raise rates this autumn but would consider an increase early next year if the market remained stable, he said.
Weiden added: "September was normal but not particularly heated up. We expect more business for October and November."
Korean Airlines has dropped plans for a five to ten percent ex-Germany rate rise but cut back on spot prices after Lufthansa decided not to change its Korea rates.
Robert Instinsky, KAL cargo sales manager Germany, said September was a "fairly average" month which generated a slight plus after a record July and August.
"We were relatively full and had an average load factor of 90 per cent," he said.
The market was now waiting to see whether export tonnages increased in October but early signs were not over-encouraging, he added.
Lufthansa's Pfaff said: "Japan and Korea are both growing very well. Japan has increased at the highest rate of any top destination."
Rates to China vary widely from the prime rates asked by Lufthansa and Cathay Pacific to lower prices demanded by carriers such as China Eastern.
Frank Wortmann, managing director of Penta Shipping, cargo sales agent for Air China, said his volumes to China have risen since a 10-15 percent rates cut on September 1.
"The rates cuts has been welcomed by the market and we are now more competitive than before," he said.
"The Chinese market boomed last year but after customs charges went up at the start of this year, the market fell away," he added.
Market rates to the USA, in particular to Miami and Los Angeles as gateways to holiday regions, have risen as additional summer passenger capacity is taken off the market.
Lufthansa sales and marketing manager Pfaff said the airline is seeing steady single-figure growth in volumes to North America.
He described market rates as showing a stable upwards trend but confirmed there had been no major increases by carriers.

Danita Waterfall, Delta Air Lines regional director cargo sales and services Europe, said: "The whole market is down but we do not want to dump prices. The (rates) level is the same as before the summer."
Delta aimed to market its ongoing product and service improvements such as its guaranteed same-day delivery and respond to market changes more rapidly in future, she said.
United Airlines cargo sales manager Germany, Robert Blythe, said he made no October rates changes but noted the price slump lasting most of the year appeared to have halted.

He added: "More charter airlines are filling their cargo space very aggressively. They are not moving big volumes but they can do whatever they like with prices because they do not have to meet revenue targets."
Competition to Latin America is heating up with the October 5 launch of three times a week MD-11 passenger services from Frankfurt to Sao Paulo by Brazilian airline VASP.
The new Swissair weekly DC 10-30 freighter from Basle to Sao Paulo with a capacity of about 65 tonnes has also made an impact on the German market, sources said.
This additional capacity has tended to equal out the Lufthansa five percent hike on certain weight categories and a Varig general price rise of nearly five percent from October 1.
The Germany sales manager of one Latin American carrier described business as "booming" and said he was very positive about the rest of the year.
Lan Chile cargo manager Europe, Martin Rehs, said the Chilean national carrier would not increase rates this autumn since it kept them fairly stable through the summer.
"Lan Chile comes on to the market as a relatively high price carrier. We will wait and see, but the prime aim is not to raise rates but to increase tonnage," he said.
Lufthansa's Pfaff said Latin America was showing a double-figure plus for the airline with good growth for Argentina, Chile and Mexico.
Rates to Africa are holding stable as tonnage grows steadily, market observers said.
South African Airways SAA.CN said it has not increased rates this autumn but believed a downward trend had now stabilised.
The airline's Germany cargo sales chief, Hugo Duchemin, said: "The market is fairly stable at the moment. Rates are stable from our point of view.
"The rand has recovered somewhat and I expect growth to match general economic growth in Germany," he added.
SAA was aimed to maintain the levels of ex-Germany prices and was not trying to pressurise competitors on prices, he added.
Lufthansa's Pfaff said freighter services to Johannesburg were full but heavy competition meant rates were under strong pressure.

Alitalia sales manager Dirk Steiger claimed he had gained a 35 percent share of the Germany-South African market among non-German European carriers by selling the airline's daily MD-11 combi flight from Rome. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
